idiom_name: thin Play action + service class or pure function (ScalaTest)
implementation_notes: In Scala the humble form is a controller action that parses the request, calls a service class or pure function, and renders the result, with ScalaTest driving the service directly (and a hand-written stub of the service trait, or Mockito, when delegation itself is verified). What replaces the classic structure is the trait plus a plain implementation: dependencies are constructor parameters, so a suite constructs the service with fakes and no application is started. Keep the action where it only adapts the framework (content negotiation, JSON mapping) and move any branch that decides business behaviour out of it.
pitfalls: Action composition and filters run inside the framework pipeline and hide decisions (defaults, validation) where tests reach them only through a running application; keep them to cross-cutting plumbing.
Futures run on the framework's execution context, so a controller returning Future[Result] needs an injected context (or a synchronous test context) or the tests become timing-dependent.
Implicit parameter lists can silently resolve a production dependency in a test; prefer explicit constructor parameters for the service so the suite shows what it uses.
